DISCOVERY, 612, APPEARANCES: JOHN M. LE BLANC, ESQ. FOR DEFENDANT/OPPOSING PARTY. NO OTHER APPEARANCES. TENTATIVE RULING ADOPTED. PLAINTIFF'S MOTION TO COMPEL THE DEPOSITION OF BLUE SHIELD IS DENIED. DEFENDANT OBJECTED TO CATEGORY 4 OF THE NOTICE OF DEPOSITION. NO MOTION HAS BEEN MADE TO OVERRULE THAT OBJECTION, AND NO AGREEMENT WAS MADE BY DEFENDANT TO RESPOND TO THAT CATEGORY. THE AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE A SCHEDULE OF BENEFITS WAS NOT AN AGREEMENT TO ADDITIONAL TESTIMONY BY A PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE. THE DEPOSTION WAS TERMINATED WITHOUT AN AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE FURTHER PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE TESTIMONY. AS THE MOTION SEEKS FURTHER PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE TESTIMONY REGARDING THE DENIAL OF THE CLAIM AND APPEAL, THE MOTION SEEKS PERCIPIENT WITNESS TESTIMONY, NOT PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE TESTIMONY. THAT TESTIMONY MUST BE OBTAINED FROM INDIVIDUAL WITNESSES. PLAINTIFF CANNOT DESIGNATE DEFENDANT'S PERSON MOST KNOWLEDGEABLE. ALL REQUESTS FOR SANCTIONS ARE DENIED. COMM: EVERETT A. HEWLETT
